Every time I’m fortunate enough to present to Elon, I’m blown away by how dedicated he is to learn about the technical progress and how much he cares about the low-level details while respecting each engineer’s work. Elon is so unique and It’s such an honor to work for him.

quoted.text:
In case anyone is curious:

We’ve had a ~pixel-perfect world model since last year, which is critical for synthetic data generation. 

The (much) smaller version of that in the car is a conditional mean-flow model, based on the recent sequence of Tesla Universal Vision Encoder features, which are the same ones that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions. 

We fork off from these UVE features, then run a separate ~1B diffusion model. This takes in the previous reality-view generation with added noise and then denoises it to the current visualization. 

It then produces a small video chunk (8 images at 36 fps, at the resolution of the UI screen). This work is done by 1/2 of a TRIP engine every UVE frame at 18 hz and is spread over 4 cycles. 

Currently, the latency is a bit high due to compute constraints, but we have ways to interleave newer UVE features along the diffusion transformer layers to cut roughly 35% of the latency.

retweet.text:
I've been using @bot to help my fiancée and me plan our wedding, and it honestly feels like we have a hired full-time wedding planner.

Over the last month, it helped us figure out our hotel room block.

It found 15 hotels within 35 minutes of our venue, handled all the email correspondence, and got proposals with the details we needed to decide.

Then it created a comparison sheet with the criteria we cared about and recommended a shortlist.

Once we picked one, it helped us review the contract, negotiated with the hotel, and even signed it (w/ my permission, of course).

The day after we signed,  @bot proactively researched a shortlist of shuttle services and welcome-party venues, with emails already drafted for my review.

I can't imagine planning a wedding without it. It's truly an amazing time to be alive.

Iceland is considered “the most gender-equal country in the world” but it doesn’t seem “equal” to me… Currently, they have a female President, Prime Minister, the head of every political party is a woman and the majority of cabinet is women. 68.8% of students who graduated college last year were women. This list goes on about how “gender equality” actually seems to mean female dominance today.

Yesterday I spoke with the former First Lady of Iceland. She did seem concerned about the college student stat, but she insisted there was still so much to do to fight for gender equality for women there.

I think it might be time to look at the disadvantages of both sexes when it comes to addressing “gender equality.” No?
